messages:
security-bot: [ALERT] High-risk pod started in prod-asia1: namespace=payments, pod=payments-worker-7fc9d, image=docker.redwood.internal/payments-worker:latest (sha256:ab12cd34...). hostPID=true hostNetwork=true. Link: https://alerts.redwood/alert/1764135823

maya: Noted. Oncall, can you confirm node and cordon?

oncall-sre: Cordon in progress. Node is gke-prod-asia1-n4. Running: `kubectl cordon gke-prod-asia1-n4`

oncall-sre: Also taking a snapshot of `/var/log/containers` and `/var/log/pods`, not rebooting.

nik: Stop any automated restarts. Scale down the deployment if it's a replicaSet we control: `kubectl -n payments scale deploy/payments-worker --replicas=0`

elena: Quick note — I ran `cosign verify` against the digest we pulled and verification failed (no valid signature). Registry manifest shows push from CI user `ci-bot@ci.redwood` at 02:11 UTC which is odd.

maya: Good catch. Do we have registry audit logs? Can someone list recent pushes and IPs?

sam: Pulling registry logs now. Found a push at 02:10 from IP 34.82.191.12 via service account token that maps to `ci-bot`. That token's last used at 02:10 too.

nik: Treat as compromised until proven otherwise. Immediate actions: 1) revoke `ci-bot` token/credentials 2) rotate any KMS keys that could have been used to sign images or decrypt secrets 3) block node outbound egress to external registry endpoints from that subnet.

elena: We should also check KMS audit logs for recent sign/unwrap operations. I see a couple of unwraps around 02:09-02:12 — tagging those requests.

maya: I'll open an incident ticket (INC-2026) and notify CISO and legal. We should prepare a short internal comms: impacted services = payments, possible scope = image tampering, no confirmed host compromise yet.

oncall-sre: Forensics: I've captured `tar` of `/proc`, `mount`, `ps aux` (frozen), and container filesystem diff. Uploading to secure bucket now. Do not redeploy to this node.

elena: Hunt: run `kubectl get pods -A -o=custom-columns='N:metadata.name,IM:spec.containers[*].image'` and match by digest across clusters. Also search ECR/registry for other tags pushed at ~02:10 with similar manifest size.

sam: Registry team recommends quarantining the image by marking manifest as deprecated and blocking pulls by digest. Doing that now.

nik: Comms: Prepare customer-safe blurb in case it escalates. Post-incident: enforce image signature verification in admission controller (cosign verification), enable stricter PodSecurity admission (no hostPID/hostNetwork), and require image pulls by digest only.

maya: Agreed. Action items assigned in INC-2026: revoke creds (sam), rotate KMS (elena), node quarantine + snapshots (oncall-sre), global image hunt (nik + elena), postmortem + remediation (maya).

elena: One more — check cluster audit logs for anomalous `kubectl exec` or `create pod` requests around 02:00-03:00 UTC. If we find lateral movement, escalate to IR team.

nik: For now, no evidence of container escape in node snapshots but preserve artifacts. We'll update in 30m or earlier if new intel. :eyes:
